_comment: Template for tools/discord_bot/config.local.json - copy it and fill in real values ON THE BOX. The real file is gitignored because the token is a credential equal to the bot itself: anyone holding it can run every slash command below, including map changes and match restarts. Get the ids by enabling Discord Settings > Advanced > Developer Mode, then right-clicking a server / channel / role and choosing Copy ID. There is deliberately NO rcon password here - the bot reads it from dedicated.cfg so there is one copy to rotate.

_notes.adminRoleId: Required. Gates every command that changes the server (say, map, restart, pause, resume). Read-only commands (status, players) are open to the guild.
_notes.relayChannelId: The ONE channel whose messages are relayed into the game. Leave empty to disable the relay entirely. Every other channel is ignored.
_notes.relayRoleId: Optional. Empty means anyone who can post in the relay channel can talk to players in game - fine for a private channel, wrong for a public one. Set it to require a role.
_notes.voiceLogChannelId: The channel that receives voice activity cards (joined / left / moved, and who did it when a moderator moved or disconnected someone). EMPTY = the feature is off AND its gateway intent is not requested, which is the point: never ask Discord for an intent a disabled feature would use. Attributing a move or disconnect to an actor additionally needs the View Audit Log permission - without it the cards still post, they just never carry a By line, and the bot says which mode it is in in its service log at startup.
_notes.quietActorIds: Discord user ids whose ACTIONS are never named. The event is still logged in full, only the By line is withheld - intended for the owner, whose routine moderation is noise rather than news. It is not a mute: to keep someone's own joins and leaves out of the channel you would need a different filter.
_notes.voiceLogBots: false (default) ignores bots moving in and out of voice, which is almost always what you want since music and recording bots churn. true logs them like anyone else.
_notes.presence: true (default) puts a live line under the bot in the member list: 'Watching 3 players on Nuketown', or 'an empty server' / 'the server (offline)' / 'the server (status unknown)' with the dot going idle or red to match. Set false to turn it off. It needs NO intent, NO permission and NO portal setting, which is why it defaults on. It counts HUMANS only, because bot fill would otherwise make it read busy around the clock. Note this is bot presence (gateway op 3), NOT Rich Presence: the Developer Portal's Rich Presence Art Assets are published by a game client over local IPC, which BO1/Plutonium does not do, so no server-side feature can reach them.
_notes.statusJson: Optional override for the status projection presence reads (default C:\inetpub\wwwroot\live\status.json, written every ~5s by GF-StatusService). Presence deliberately reads this FILE rather than polling rcon: the panel is the box's single rcon pacer and a permanent 20s poller for a cosmetic feature is exactly what the project rule forbids.
_notes.messageLogChannelId: Channel that receives DELETE / EDIT / bulk-purge cards. EMPTY = off, and the privileged MESSAGE_CONTENT intent is then not requested. ⚠ MAKE THIS CHANNEL PRIVATE: to report a deleted message the bot has to have kept it, so this channel will contain things people deleted on purpose. Needs MESSAGE CONTENT enabled in the Developer Portal, plus View Audit Log to name a moderator who deleted someone else's message (a self-delete writes no audit entry at all, which is why an unattributed card means the author did it).
_notes.messageLogMedia: true (default) buffers attachments in MEMORY while a message is alive and re-uploads them if it is deleted - the only way to log media, since a deleted message's CDN link cannot be refreshed. Capped in lib/attachments.js: 8MB per file, 64MB total, 15 minute TTL, nothing written to disk and nothing surviving a restart. Set false to log filenames only.
_notes.messageLogIgnoreChannels: Channel ids never logged. The message-log channel itself is ALWAYS excluded automatically - without that the bot's own cards would be logged and a purge in there would recurse.
_notes.memberLogChannelId: Channel that receives JOIN / LEAVE / rename cards. EMPTY = off. ⚠ Needs the privileged SERVER MEMBERS intent enabled in the Developer Portal. A leave card cannot tell a leave from a kick or a ban - the gateway does not say - so it reports what is known rather than guessing.
_notes.memberLogNewAccountDays: Join cards flag an account younger than this many days (default 7), read from the user id itself, so it costs no API call. A raid and ban-evasion signal, not a verdict: nothing is kicked, a human decides.
_notes.modChannelId: Channel that receives moderation cards, and the switch for the whole link/media filter. EMPTY = off. Not optional decoration: moderation with no log is moderation nobody can review or appeal. Needs MANAGE MESSAGES to delete and MODERATE MEMBERS to time out. ⚠ The escalation stops at TIMEOUT - nothing here kicks or bans, deliberately, because a false positive that bans a real player costs more than any spam wave.
_notes.modBlockedExtensions: File extensions refused outright, EMPTY = use the built-in list (executables and script types: exe, bat, ps1, jar, apk, vbs and friends). Checked on the LAST extension, so 'screenshot.png.exe' is caught. ⚠ Cannot see inside an archive: a .zip full of malware passes.
_notes.modMaxAttachmentMB: Refuse attachments larger than this. 0 = no size rule.
_notes.modAllowedDomains: Non-empty turns links into an ALLOWLIST: any message containing a host not on this list is removed. Subdomains are covered, so 'youtube.com' allows 'www.youtube.com'. Leave empty to use modBlockedDomains instead.
_notes.modBlockedDomains: Denylist, used only when modAllowedDomains is empty. Both empty = links are unrestricted.
_notes.modLinkMinAccountDays: Accounts younger than this many days may not post links (0 = off). The single most effective anti-spam rule there is, and it is checked BEFORE the domain lists so an allow-listed host cannot smuggle a fresh account past it.
_notes.modExemptRoles: Role ids never filtered. The admin role is always exempt without being listed.
_notes.modExemptChannels: Channel ids never filtered. The log channels are always exempt automatically - our own cards quote removed content and would otherwise trip the filters that produced them.
_notes.modStrikes: Strikes inside modStrikeWindowMinutes before a timeout is applied (default 3). Strikes live in memory and reset on restart, which is a deliberate amnesty rather than an oversight.
_notes.modTimeoutMinutes: How long a timeout lasts once the strike threshold is hit (default 10).
_notes.automodChannelId: Where Discord's NATIVE AutoMod hits are logged, and the /automod command's home. Falls back to modChannelId. ⚠ Needs the AUTO_MODERATION_EXECUTION intent (1<<21, NOT privileged, requested automatically) plus the MANAGE SERVER permission - without the permission the feature is blind and says so in the service log. This module REPORTS Discord's rules and never edits them: rule changes belong in Server Settings where an owner can see what they do.
_notes.securityChannelId: Channel for the raid alarm and alerts on dangerous guild changes (role permissions granted, a BOT added, a webhook created, server settings edited). Falls back to modChannelId. EMPTY = off. ⚠ Needs the privileged SERVER MEMBERS intent for the raid alarm, and View Audit Log for the rest. ⚠ It ALERTS and never acts: every automated response to a raid has a failure mode worse than the raid itself, so the bot's job is noticing within seconds and the decision stays with a human.
_notes.securityAlertRoleId: Role pinged for CRITICAL alerts only (default: nobody). ⚠ The ONLY place in this bot that can ping - every other card sets allowed_mentions parse:[] so a mention chip notifies nobody. 'Someone just granted a role Administrator' is worth a phone buzzing at 3am; nothing else here is.
_notes.securityRaidJoins: Joins inside securityRaidWindowSeconds before the raid alarm fires (default 5 in 60s).
_notes.securityRaidCooldownMinutes: Minimum gap between raid alarms (default 10), so a wave produces one alert rather than one per joiner.
_notes.presenceMapArt: false (default) = the bot's profile shows text only. true adds the current map as the activity's large image. ⚠ UNPROVEN: the gateway docs do not state whether Discord renders activity ASSETS for a BOT's own presence, and it cannot be tested from code - uploading an asset needs the Developer Portal, because the API answers a bot token with 'Bots cannot use this endpoint' (403 / 20001). ⚠ The key is an ASSET NAME uploaded under Rich Presence > Art Assets, NOT a URL - this is the one place a gunfight.us image does NOT work, unlike an embed thumbnail which takes any public https URL. Name each asset after the ENGINE map id (mp_nuked), which is what status.json already carries.
